svg.title: Reusable Bilateral FX Spot Trade via a Shared ERC-20 Settlement Router Each example trade: Party A receives BASE_QTY base tokens and pays QUOTE_QTY quote tokens

g.text: Reusable Bilateral FX Spot Trade via a Shared ERC-20 Settlement Router
Each example trade: Party A receives BASE_QTY base tokens and pays QUOTE_QTY quote tokens
The framework route is a proposal, not implemented Solidity.
Select one factory deployment: standalone OR framework-aware.
The proposed factory extends AbstractProductFactory and directly deploys FX trade instances.
It owns its router; it does not forward through the standalone factory.
[Proposed framework route: publish an FX product definition once]
check IProductFactory via ERC-165, configured registry,
payload schema and required resource types
Registry and finalized text resources are already deployed.
No indication assignment or trade-request workflow is required for this route.
Resource validation calls are summarized above.
Allowances are given early to the deployed settlementRouter.
Trade instances created through the selected factory settle through its settlementRouter.
Tokens must transfer the exact requested amount synchronously.
Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens are outside this example's supported scope.
For this sign configuration, Party A authorizes quote-token spending
and Party B authorizes base-token spending. Any remaining allowance can be used
by later trades on this instance or other trade instances registered with the same router.
Replenish allowances before later settlements when necessary.
Create and register one reusable instance
require caller is PartyA or PartyB
require registry owner and fulfillable definition
require caller and common.productRegistry match Registry
store immutable tokens, parties, and Router
require Trade has code and is not registered
emit TradeCreated(Trade, PartyA, BaseToken, QuoteToken, PartyA, PartyB)
Issuance creates and registers the reusable instance once.
Later trades use that same instance directly, without registry issuance.
Issuance does not authorize a trade or move tokens.
The no-request route does not automatically check client eligibility.
The existing party/operator agreement below remains required.
The current registry does not require IProduct metadata getters on the trade instance.
The router permanently registers the instance and consumes trade IDs individually.
The trade instance fixes tokens, parties and router; amounts and terms belong to each trade.
Either fixed party may incept. The example below consistently uses Party A.
The arrows below show direct participant calls.
A participant may call setTradeOperator(operator, true) on this trade instance.
A's approved operator may submit inception or cancellation; B's may confirm.
Caller identity does not change either participant or the amount perspective.
Approval is checked at execution and may be revoked with false.
Operator approval also applies to future trades on this instance until revoked.
ERC-20 allowances alone do not authorize trade actions.
[Successive trades on this instance: one pending quote at a time]
ERC-6123 inception generates a fresh trade ID
validate nonzero, opposite-sign legs; reject int256 minimum
On-chain clients use the returned ID. Off-chain clients read TradeIncepted
from their transaction receipt; do not predict an ID before submission.
The local demo reads tradeId() after successful inception with no intervening trade.
Confirmation and cancellation include the actual generated ID.
Sign convention from the inceptor's perspective:
The rate follows from the two exact amounts and token decimals.
Each trade can use different amounts and textual terms.
Resolve the quote through ERC-6123 confirmation or cancellation
same tradeId, PartyA, PartyB, same tradeData,
match pending tradeId; require phase == Incepted
match original signed amounts and terms
Permanent registration authenticates the factory-created caller.
Consume this ID before external token calls to prevent duplicate settlement.
The trade instance guards inception, confirmation and cancellation against reentrancy,
including attempts to start another trade during the current settlement.
The included tokens return true, as shown below.
The router also accepts empty return data. A revert, false return,
or invalid ABI-encoded boolean causes settlement to revert.
Base leg: Party B delivers base to Party A
update balances and decrease finite allowance
Quote leg: Party A delivers quote to Party B
update balances and decrease finite allowance
Settlement occurs in one transaction submitted by Party B or its approved operator.
If validation or either token call fails, all effects of that transaction are undone.
For the open quote shown here, phase remains Incepted and consumedTrade = false:
Party B may retry, or Party A may cancel, directly or through their approved operators.
A rejected call for a closed ID preserves its terminal state and any newer trade.
same tradeId, PartyA, PartyB, same tradeData,
match pending tradeId; require phase == Incepted
Cancellation transfers no tokens and preserves balances and ERC-20 allowances.
If the router call fails, cancellation reverts completely.
This trade ID is permanently closed; another inception generates a fresh ID.
No factory call, router re-registration or registry issuance is needed.
Latest getters and the ERC-8100 XML view follow the latest trade.
getTrade(id) retains each trade's terms and phase; closed records remain unchanged.
An open quote is withdrawn through cancelTrade by the inceptor or its approved operator.
There is no clock-based expiry; transaction order determines which terminal action succeeds.
Settled and Canceled are final for one ID, while the instance remains reusable.
Router registration persists; per-ID consumption flags and stored records are never reset.
The request/confirm/cancelTradeTermination methods are unsupported and revert.
